title: Waymaker Artemis B: QLoRA SFT of Gemma 4 E4B-it on reviewed classification labels
status_detail: Prepared on 2026-10-19 in Mission 001. Not trained: benchmark v0 has no train split, there is no GPU on the preparation machine, and paid training is not authorised. train_qlora.py refuses this config today (train file missing).
hypothesis: QLoRA SFT on human-reviewed, benchmark-format classification examples (structured labels only, no legal facts) raises text-only subcode_exact and procedure_fine over arm A on test and adversarial_holdout, with a 95% CI that excludes 0, without any increase in parent-for-subcode substitutions or visa/stay scope mixes.
null_hypothesis: SFT does not improve on arm A beyond the CI, or it improves the averages while adding critical errors. Then prompting (arm A) or the rules (B-fixed) are enough and the adapter is discarded.

baselines.what: Same base model, same prompt, same decoding, no adapter.
Best deterministic classifier after cheap rule fixes.

base_model.license_note: Apache-2.0 per HF cardData; keep the licence text and NOTICE with any distributed adapter. Gemma Prohibited Use Policy applicability unresolved (models.md §4, §8).
base_model.loader_note: Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration checkpoint; AutoModelForImageTextToText + AutoProcessor is the documented Gemma 4 path. CUDA training remains unexecuted; validate adapters on the pinned checkpoint before training.

secondary_model.note: E2B is an explicitly selected development profile only. Keep its adapters and metrics separate; it never replaces the canonical E4B foundation.

train.note: EMPTY: benchmark v0 has dev, test and adversarial_holdout only, and no train split. A train split must be authored as validated benchmark-format examples with split 'train' (11-dataset-governance.md), split by case template so no template appears on both sides, reviewed (critical labels human_verified), and then built with training/build_sft_dataset.py. Target size 1,500-3,000 reviewed examples (training-distill.md §4.2 arm B, INFERRED for Artemis).

leakage_guard.why: Template siblings that differ in one status code share most word 3-grams (about 0.6 Jaccard for a six-token question, INFERRED); 0.5 refuses them, and the fix is a re-split by case template (training-distill.md §4.6), never a higher threshold.

label_rules: One SFT record per question. The runner asks one prompt and one 7-key schema for both Artemis tasks, so a train question needs both its status_procedure_classification and its entity_date_extraction example (same exact question text and payload code); a question with only one label is refused, never completed with a guess.

The classification label must state current_status and target_status (null allowed) and needs_clarification (true or false) explicitly; dates come from the entity label. not_status_tokens and status_codes are scoring labels, not target keys.
The target is that 7-key object as compact JSON in the runner's schema key order; no reasoning text, no evidence text, no legal content.
Critical examples need label_review.status human_verified with a named reviewer and date; disputed and unreviewed labels are refused.
teacher_generated examples are refused in this arm.

prompt.defined_in: waymaker_ai/evaluation/baselines/model.py (build_messages, system_prompt, DECODING) and waymaker_ai/evaluation/predictions.py (model_output_schema); sft_dataset.prompt_sha256 hashes all three
prompt.note: Training and evaluation use the runner's own openai_compatible request: one system prompt and one 7-key schema for both Artemis tasks, user message = question (prefixed by the UI payload code when present). A change to the runner's prompt, schema or decoding changes this hash and the config stops loading.

training.data_format: TRL conversational prompt-completion records (prompt = system + user, completion = assistant JSON)

load_in_4bit.why: QLoRA keeps the frozen base in 4 bits so E4B fits one 16-24 GB GPU (training-distill.md §2.1 QLoRA row; models.md §6).

bnb_4bit_quant_type.why: NF4 is the QLoRA data type and the arm B setting in training-distill.md §4.2.

bnb_4bit_use_double_quant.why: Double-quantised constants are assumed by the models.md §6 VRAM rule (about 0.6-0.65 GB per billion parameters).

compute_dtype.why: bf16 where the GPU supports it (L4, A100); fp16 on a T4, which has no native bf16. The old scaffold hard-codes bf16 (knowledge-platform.md §4 defect 3).

r.why: Arm B setting in training-distill.md §4.2 (Unsloth LoRA guide); the old scaffold's r=8 is an ablation to try only if r=16 overfits dev.

dropout.why: Not set in the notes (INFERRED): light regularisation for a train set of a few thousand short examples; try 0.0 if dev loss stalls.

target_modules.why: All linear projections of the language model (training-distill.md §4.2). Whether all seven names exist in Gemma 4 is UNVERIFIED (models.md §8); train_qlora.py targets only language-model projections: matches inside a vision or audio tower are excluded and listed in run_record.json, and it refuses if a configured name matches no language-model layer.

bias.why: Only the adapter matrices train; nothing else in the base changes.

learning_rate.why: 2e-4, the training-distill.md §4.2 setting (Unsloth guide; TRL SFT docs).

num_train_epochs.why: The notes give 1-3 epochs; 2 is the midpoint, and dev loss alone decides a move to 1 or 3 before test is scored.

max_seq_length.why: Questions are capped at 2,000 characters (example.schema.json); the runner's system prompt is about 1,400 characters and the JSON target is short, so 2048 tokens leaves room; 2048 is also the length behind the models.md §6 VRAM rule. train_qlora.py refuses any record that would be truncated (token counts INFERRED until measured).

per_device_train_batch_size.why: Micro-batch 1 is the models.md §6 VRAM assumption and fits a 16 GB T4.

gradient_accumulation_steps.why: Effective batch 16 (INFERRED): about 90-190 optimiser steps per epoch for 1,500-3,000 examples, enough for a readable loss curve.

optimizer.why: Paged 8-bit AdamW on the adapters is the models.md §6 VRAM assumption.

lr_scheduler.why: Common default (INFERRED); decays smoothly from the 2e-4 peak.

warmup_ratio.why: Common default (INFERRED): about 3% of steps of warmup avoids an early spike at 2e-4.

gradient_checkpointing.why: Part of the models.md §6 VRAM rule; trades speed for activation memory.

loss.why: Loss on the assistant JSON only (training-distill.md §4.2: TRL completion_only_loss VERIFIED). Prompt-completion records avoid depending on chat-template generation markers.

seeds.why: Three seeds per arm, reported as mean with a 95% bootstrap CI (training-distill.md §4.2 controls).

training.outputs: One LoRA adapter per seed under training/runs/<config id>/<primary|secondary>-seed<k>/adapter (git-ignored) plus run_record.json (config sha256, SFT file sha256, base revision, package versions, GPU, dtype, wall-clock, train loss).
training.smoke_run: Before training: train_qlora.py --model primary --seed 1 --max-steps 5 on the pinned E4B. Confirm loader, template, targets, adapter save/reload and package versions. E2B is a separate explicitly selected development run and does not validate E4B. Smoke adapters are not evaluated.

hardware.assumption: One 16-24 GB NVIDIA GPU (compute class C1, training-distill.md §2.0). L4 24 GB is the comfortable fit; T4 16 GB is borderline for E4B and runs in fp16.
hardware.vram_estimate: Unexecuted engineering estimate: begin E4B QLoRA on 24 GB CUDA with sequence 2048 and checkpointing. Smaller-memory vendor recipes need separate validation; see WAYMAKER-ARTEMIS-FINETUNING-PLAN.md.
fits: L4 24 GB: proposed E4B QLoRA starting point, bf16 compute; not measured.
T4 16 GB: E4B may OOM; fp16 compute only. Stop or choose larger hardware. E2B requires explicit development selection and separate results.

compute.note: Local or free GPU only. Managed fine-tuning APIs (Together, Fireworks) and rented GPUs are paid endpoints and are refused by train_qlora.py. No --i-understand-this-may-cost-money flag exists, because local GPUs need none and paid endpoints are refused outright.

cost.basis: Training tokens: 1,500-3,000 examples x about 600 tokens x 2 epochs = 1.8-3.6M per seed, 5.4-10.8M for 3 seeds (token count INFERRED). At the cost.md §7 assumption of 1,500-3,000 tokens/s for an 8B-class QLoRA on one A100-80GB this is 0.5-2 GPU-hours, about $0.9-3.6 at RunPod Secure $1.79/h, plus 30-100% for failed runs and evaluation (cost.md §7), plus three arm-A-style evaluation passes. $0 on a local GPU, free Colab T4 or Kaggle (slower, fp16). Colab Pro is $9.99/month if a T4 is not enough.
cost.dominant_cost: Human review of the train labels, not GPU time (cost.md §7, last bullet).
sources: research-notes/cost.md §6: RunPod Secure A100-80GB $1.79/h, L4 $0.59/h (VERIFIED, accessed 2026-10-19)
research-notes/cost.md §7: worked example, throughput assumption and the 30-100% overhead (INFERRED)

serving: vLLM with --enable-lora serving the base at the pinned revision plus the seed adapter, JSON-schema structured outputs.
llama.cpp llama-server with the adapter converted to GGUF, for T4-only setups (UNVERIFIED for Gemma 4 adapters).

decoding.why: Same as arm A; differences must come from the adapter only.

evaluation.split_discipline: Epoch count and checkpoint choice use dev only; test and adversarial_holdout are scored once per seed.
metrics: subcode_exact (a parent in the subcode field or a parent fallback is wrong)
flags parent_fallback + parent_in_subcode_field (critical; CLE-4): count must be 0
procedure_coarse (via contracts.FINE_TO_COARSE; items with no coarse equivalent are reported as not scorable)
flag procedure_scope_mixed (critical; CLE-3: a visa-scope procedure for a stay question or the reverse): count must be 0
not_status_token_respected and flag code_from_non_code_token ('a 3 month' must not become A-3)
structured-output validity rate (answers with no schema violation)
per adversarial class and per language (ko, en, other) breakdown
evaluation.reporting: Mean over 3 seeds with a 95% bootstrap CI; paired comparison against arm A on the same items.

gates.condition: A train split exists; the dataset validator passes on it; every critical label is human_verified; the leakage guard reports 0 pairs above max_overlap against dev, test and adversarial_holdout; the SFT file is a byte-identical fresh build.
gates.source: training-distill.md §4.6 and §4.7 G0; 11-dataset-governance.md; enforced by waymaker_ai/distillation/preflight.py

gates.condition: Evaluation splits frozen with a committed hash manifest before the first scored run.
gates.on_fail: Do not score test or adversarial_holdout.

gates.condition: Arm B starts only if arm A and B-fixed were scored on dev and B-fixed is below the 12-evaluation-methodology.md target on text-only subcode_exact or procedure_fine.
gates.on_fail: Do not train; keep the rules.

gates.condition: The runner's flags parent_fallback, parent_in_subcode_field and procedure_scope_mixed occur 0 times on test and adversarial_holdout for every seed, and no metric is worse than arm A beyond its CI.
gates.on_fail: NO-GO: the arm ends. Thresholds are never relaxed to let an arm pass.

gates.condition: subcode_exact or procedure_fine improves over arm A on test with a 95% bootstrap CI lower bound above 0, and adversarial_holdout is not worse.
Structured-output validity is 1.0 (no schema violation) under constrained decoding.
200 stratified outputs read by two reviewers, agreement measured, every disagreement adjudicated.
gates.on_fail: NO-GO for any use beyond offline research.

gates.condition: p95 latency fits the routing budget inside the Quick Answer timeout.
gates.threshold: p95 well under 7000 ms; exact budget from 12-evaluation-methodology.md

limitations: The TRL / PEFT / bitsandbytes calls in train_qlora.py were written against the TRL v1.16.0 documentation the notes cite but were never executed (no GPU, no packages installed).
Token counts, throughput and VRAM figures are estimates (INFERRED) until the smoke run measures them.
Only one primary base model is pinned; a Korean-native alternative (Kanana-2-3B) is out of scope for this config (models.md §5).
